questions.worked_solution:
We factor the numerator and denominator and cancel any factors that they have in common.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3x+9z}{6x-15z} & =\frac{3(x+3z)}{3(2x-5z)} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{3}\cdot (x+3z)}{\cancel{3}\cdot (2x-5z)} \\  & =\frac{x+3z}{2x-5z}\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: What is $\dfrac {2x + 4} {2}$ reduced to lowest terms?
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We factor the numerator and denominator and cancel any factors that they have in common.

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{2x+4}{2} & =\frac{2(x+2)}{2} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{2}(x+2)}{\cancel{2}\cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{x+2}{1} \\  & =x+2\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
